title: B2B Video Marketing: A Full-Funnel Campaign System
summary: Choose a B2B paid social agency that connects creative and targeting to qualified pipeline. Define CRM handoffs, lead quality and reporting before launch.
body_markdown:
## How should the agency turn a broad audience into a useful brief?


Start with a buying situation rather than a job-title list alone. Identify the task the person is trying to complete, the obstacle that makes it difficult and the product evidence relevant to that obstacle. Then distinguish the person experiencing the problem from the person approving a purchase.


For an illustrative expense-management product, an employee may care about submitting a receipt without retyping information. A finance manager may care about reviewing exceptions. A business owner may need to understand how the new process will be introduced. These are three communication briefs around one product, not permission to invent a different capability for each audience.


Ask the agency to write one sentence connecting each audience to an action: “A finance manager who is evaluating approval workflows should see the exception-review demonstration and request a focused walkthrough.” If the sentence requires several unrelated promises, narrow the brief. The exercise helps expose an audience definition that is too broad to produce useful creative.


Use your own sales and product evidence to prioritize those situations. Record where each objection came from and whether it represents a recurring question or one unusual conversation. The agency can propose a hypothesis where evidence is limited, but it should label that hypothesis and explain what the campaign could help you learn.


## What does a practical lead-quality feedback loop look like?


Agree a small set of disposition reasons with sales before reviewing lead quality. Examples for a proposed workflow include relevant company and use case, wrong use case, no current project, unable to contact and duplicate inquiry. Adapt the categories to your business; do not require the agency to infer qualification from a name or email alone.


Consider an illustrative pilot with 30 inquiries. Suppose sales has reviewed 18 and left 12 untouched. Of the reviewed inquiries, six fit the intended use case, eight do not and four have not yet responded. Reporting six qualified inquiries out of 30 without explaining the unreviewed group would obscure the state of the follow-up process. Keep the categories and observation date visible.


Next, connect the reasons to a decision. If the wrong-use-case group misunderstood a feature, examine the ad and landing page for the wording that created that impression. If suitable inquiries are waiting for follow-up, assign that operational task before rewriting every ad. Neither pattern alone proves that the campaign caused the outcome.


The useful feedback artifact is a short decision note: observed pattern, evidence, alternative explanation, next change and owner. Share only the information needed for campaign decisions and follow your company's data-handling rules. An agency report should help marketing and sales agree the next action instead of turning incomplete follow-up into an argument about lead quality.


## How should you compare two B2B agency proposals?


Normalize the commercial job before the fee. One proposal may include production and campaign management while another assumes your team supplies the ads and owns the lead handoff. Put those responsibilities beside the quote so the difference remains visible.


Ask each finalist to respond to the same sample situation. Your product team has an accurate demo, sales has recurring objections and marketing has limited editing capacity. What would the agency produce first? Who checks the product explanation? Who approves the offer? How would the campaign owner know whether the resulting inquiries match the intended situation? Request an outline of the work rather than a free completed campaign.


Compare how the teams reason about missing evidence. A confident prediction based only on a company category is less useful than a plan that names its assumptions. Look for a proposed sequence that your team can support with real inputs and a reporting method that matches your follow-up capacity.


Keep setup, ongoing service fees, production and media spend distinct. Also account for internal subject-matter review and sales follow-up. Those tasks do not disappear because an agency produces the ad. Price a combined scope against the same complete workload as a specialist arrangement.


## What should the first campaign review decide?


Use the first review to decide what is ready to continue, what needs correction and what remains unknown. Review the actual delivered ads, their destinations, the agreed campaign information and the sales dispositions available so far. Avoid filling the meeting with every metric that happens to be accessible.


For each message, ask whether it accurately described the product, attracted the intended type of inquiry and supplied a useful next step. If the evidence is too early or incomplete, record the limitation and specify the information needed for another decision. A clear unresolved question is more actionable than declaring success from activity alone.

Define the chosen scope and private fee in writing, with media spend separate. Keep any LinkedIn management, CRM implementation or broader sales operations explicitly assigned to the appropriate team.


For creative, require accurate screen captures, approved claims, a named subject-matter reviewer and a manageable revision process. ## Key takeaways


- Brief the buyer’s role, problem and next step.
- Test the CRM handoff before scaling campaigns.
- Distinguish lead volume from qualified opportunities.
- Use the[paid social scope guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/paid-social-agency) to assign ownership.


## FAQ


### Should B2B companies advertise only on LinkedIn?


Do not make that decision from the company category alone. Ask for a platform-specific audience, offer and measurement rationale, then evaluate a suitable pilot against your own business criteria.


### Is cost per lead a sufficient success metric?


Cost per lead describes one stage. Agree with sales how inquiries become reviewed, accepted, disqualified and qualified opportunities, and record the reasons for each decision. Show unreviewed leads separately. That gives the agency usable feedback about the message or offer without confusing inexpensive form submissions with useful pipeline.


### Should every B2B video ask for a demo?


Choose the next step according to the audience and offer. A focused demo can suit a product question; another brief may call for a guide, trial or technical conversation.
